import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 352

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/352](https://www.erdosproblems.com/352)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry
open scoped ProbabilityTheory

namespace Erdos352

/--
Is there some $c > 0$ such that every measurable $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of measure $\geq c$
 contains the vertices of a triangle of area 1?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem erdos_352 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > (0: ℝ), ∀ A : Set ℝ², MeasurableSet A → ℙ A ≥ c.toEReal
       → (∃ t : Affine.Triangle ℝ ℝ²,
           (∀ p : Fin 3, t.points p ∈ A) ∧
           EuclideanGeometry.triangle_area (t.points 0) (t.points 1) (t.points 2) = 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos352

reformulations.difference: The source asks for a triangle of ordinary area 1, whereas triangle_area is signed and the Lean statement requires its value to equal +1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The triangle is existentially quantified, and its vertex-membership condition is invariant under reindexing. A triangle of unsigned area 1 has signed area either +1 or -1. In the latter case, reindexing by the transposition of vertices 0 and 1 reverses the signed area and preserves affine independence and membership in A. Conversely, signed area +1 gives unsigned area 1. The equivalence for every A is proved as signed_unsigned_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: MeasurableSet A uses the Borel σ-algebra on the Euclidean plane, rather than explicitly quantifying over all Lebesgue-measurable sets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every Lebesgue-measurable A contains a Borel subset B with the same measure, including when that measure is infinite. Applying the Borel formulation to B supplies vertices in B ⊆ A. The converse follows because every Borel set is Lebesgue measurable. This preserves the same threshold c, without weakening its non-strict bound. The equivalence with NullMeasurableSet A volume is proved as borel_lebesgue_equivalence; full_reformulation also combines it with the unsigned-area formulation.
